items.title: Buddy Burton Interview, 1959-09-07
items.q: I know a fellow here in Harlem that is a good saxophone player and a clarinet player... this very boy, his name was Alec Washington

ctx.x: I was thinking you were going to say you had a wreck, but it could have been worse if you had a wreck on there.

I get up there, and here was it. One of the men dropped out on us, and Melrose says, oh, Burton says, he used to always use me to sort of this side kick, you know, along those lines, your trouble come up, and I says, well, I know a fellow here in Harlem that is a good saxophone player and a clarinet player that used to play with Ma Rainey, and he's here. And I says, I'm sure, and he made so many records with Ma Rainey, I says, he'll fit right into the picture because he knows how to handle himself and the tones…
and lives right across the street here. Oh, he's here in town now. Yeah, yeah, I seen him yesterday from a distance. Elliot?
